items.problem: First build of the migrated project failed with 6x 'error CS0579: Duplicate System.Reflection.Assembly*Attribute attribute' originating from obj\...\BackgroundSensors.AssemblyInfo.cs.
items.evidence: build-output.txt / session-log.txt turns 39-43: 'Build failed with 6 error(s)' then fixed at turn 40 by adding <GenerateAssemblyInfo>false</GenerateAssemblyInfo>. Confirmed the copied legacy file BackgroundTask\Properties\AssemblyInfo.cs contains [assembly: AssemblyTitle/Company/Configuration/Product/...].
items.skill_search: Grepped winui-uwp-migration for 'AssemblyInfo', 'GenerateAssemblyInfo', 'CS0579', 'Duplicate.*attribute' — no matches in SKILL.md, MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md, or any script.
items.root_cause: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 copies all *.cs from the UWP source, including the legacy Properties\AssemblyInfo.cs that every classic UWP project carries. SDK-style WinUI csproj's auto-generate the same assembly attributes (GenerateAssemblyInfo defaults true), so they are defined twice. Multi-project samples bring one AssemblyInfo.cs per sub-project, multiplying the duplicates.
items.proposed_fix: In Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1, skip copying Properties\AssemblyInfo.cs during the source-copy step; document in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md the CS0579 root cause and the <GenerateAssemblyInfo>false</GenerateAssemblyInfo> fallback for projects that must keep the legacy attributes.
items.generalizes: EVERY classic UWP (.NET) project ships Properties\AssemblyInfo.cs with assembly attributes, and EVERY SDK-style WinUI 3 target auto-generates the same attributes by default. Copying the legacy file therefore produces CS0579 on virtually every UWP->WinUI 3 migration, scaling with the number of sub-projects. Not scenario-specific.
